chapter: Prose: Sister Nivedita on Swami Vivekananda
trick: This is a portrait written by a disciple, so watch what she chooses to show. Nivedita gives us Vivekananda's ordinary moments — his talk, his laughter, his restlessness — because she is arguing that greatness showed in the daily man, not only on the platform at Chicago.

video.query: Sister Nivedita on Swami Vivekananda prose summary class 11 English

data.prompt: True or false? Mark each statement.

items.statement: Sister Nivedita was born Margaret Noble, in Ireland.
items.why: She came to India in 1898 and was given the name Nivedita, meaning 'the dedicated one', by Vivekananda.

items.statement: The piece is written as a distant, formal biography.
items.why: It is a personal recollection by someone who knew him daily, which is why it turns on small observed moments rather than dates.

items.statement: Vivekananda addressed the Parliament of Religions in Chicago in 1893.
items.why: His opening words, 'Sisters and Brothers of America', are the most quoted moment of his life.

items.statement: Nivedita presents him as a man interested only in religion.
items.why: She stresses his concern with India's poverty, education and self-respect; for him service to people was itself worship.
He founded it in 1897 in the name of his teacher, Ramakrishna Paramahamsa.

trick: A Romantic poet who wrote about lakes and daffodils is here astonished by a city — and only because it is asleep. London moves him at dawn, before the smoke and the crowds start, so the poem praises the city by catching it at the one hour it resembles nature.

video.query: Composed Upon Westminster Bridge Wordsworth sonnet explanation class 11

data.prompt: True or false? Mark each statement about the sonnet.

items.statement: The poem is a Petrarchan sonnet of fourteen lines.
items.why: It runs octave then sestet, with the turn coming as the poet moves from what he sees to what he feels.

items.statement: Wordsworth is describing London at sunrise.
items.why: The date in the title is early September 1802, and the city is caught in the early morning, before it wakes.

items.statement: He finds the city ugly compared with the countryside.
items.why: The opening claim is the opposite: earth has not anything to show more fair. That a Romantic poet says this of a city is the whole surprise of the poem.

items.statement: The city is described as wearing the morning like a garment.
items.why: The image makes the city almost a living body, which is why the closing line can speak of its mighty heart lying still.

items.statement: The poem ends with the city noisy and busy.
items.why: It ends in stillness — the houses asleep and the heart of the city not yet beating.

trick: Learn the Constitution by its borrowings and its numbers. Fundamental Rights from the USA, Directive Principles from Ireland, parliamentary government from Britain.
